collection._comment: overlap_hours widens each sitemap and feed date filter below the source's watermark; URL dedup drops what is already stored. Without it an article whose discovery date is earlier than the previous run's start is never collected. Measured 2026-09-15: DVZ and haendlerbund.de state date-only dates (read as 02:00), so nothing published after 06:00 fell inside a later window; VerkehrsRundschau lists articles hours after their lastmod, which a 2-hour intraday window never contains. All three had stored nothing new for 3-5 days while reporting ok or zero. 48 covers a date-only day plus that lag and matches a news sitemap's two-day listing. Frontpage discovery is not date-filtered and does not use it. The watermark itself is unchanged.

body_fetch._comment: Full-text sources produce ~157 items/day, so a limit of 100 could never keep up. 1000 is a safety rail, not a throttle. delay_seconds is enforced per host, not globally: tasks are interleaved across sources, so consecutive requests normally hit different publishers anyway. max_attempts counts consecutive retryable failures (a success resets it); after that many the URL is retired as unavailable and only --retry-unavailable or a changed discovery hint reopens it.

title_gate._comment: Cheap LLM check between the keyword selector and a body fetch, for title-only sources. Chosen 2026-09-11 on 247 hand-labelled candidates, three shuffled runs per model: gpt-5.4-mini at reasoning 'low' missed 1 of 69 relevant judgements and kept 2 extras, about $0.07/month at 25 items/day. With reasoning 'none' it missed 14; larger models without reasoning cost more and missed more. A dated snapshot, so the model cannot change underneath the gate. log_keep_days prunes the per-day decision logs in data/title_gate/.

body_gate._comment: Cheap LLM relevance check between a selected body and the full assessment, for news and regulatory bodies. gpt-5.6-terra since 2026-09-14, measured against gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17 on the 90 hand-labelled bodies in clients/jt-express/labels/, three trials each at reasoning 'low': both kept all 16 relevant items in every trial; terra kept 4-5 irrelevant per trial against mini's 7-8, and after the config exclusions only one of terra's (the BPEX 'Zoll' section page) can still reach the gate against about four of mini's; terra changed its verdict on 7 items across trials, mini on 11; about $2.90 a month against $1.30. A sharpened prompt was tried in the same run and rejected: it cost mini a relevant item and gained terra nothing. Terra has no dated snapshot, so every assessment payload records the model actually used, and a suspected upstream change is re-scored against the same 90 labels. One body per call. body_chars caps the text sent - the p90 body is about 7,700 characters. workers are parallel calls. limit is a safety rail per kind and run, newest first, so a backlog drains over a few runs instead of in one surprise; a normal day is about 25 news and 5 regulatory bodies.

alert_gate._comment: gpt-5.4-mini missed STALE_DAYS 2/10 at 'low' and 2/10 at 'medium' on a known bad case (2026-09-14, see src/alert_gate.py). gpt-5.6-luna was 20/20 and cheaper - no dated snapshot exists yet, so alert_decision.payload.model records the actual model per run.

report_agent._comment: The weekly assessment and report (src/report_agent/). Not the gates' model: the gates are a cheap screen in front of this, while this stage reads bodies, challenges its own first reading and writes the customer-facing Chinese, so it gets a capable model. gpt-5.6-sol has no dated snapshot published - the convention everywhere else in this file is a pinned date, and this is the one place it cannot be honoured, so a silent upstream change to 'sol' is a live risk and assessment-manifest.json records the model on every run to make it visible. Reasoning effort is per step: triage is a keep/omit call over titles, deep read and challenge are where the quality comes from. Tool-call budgets are rails, not throttles - a step that exhausts one is told to answer from what it read rather than cut off. max_stories bounds a pathological week; stories over the cap are recorded as unread, never silently dropped. Raised from 12 to 20 on 2026-09-12: a normal week clustered to 13, so 12 was a throttle rather than a rail. Cost for a full cycle is unmeasured (report_plan.md §8); the first full run over 2026-09-05..11 was 73 model calls and 80 tool calls for 381k input and 58k output tokens in 15 minutes, and tokens are counted per step in every bundle's assessment-manifest.json.

backup._comment: Daily-only while the project is in testing: the point right now is 'roll back to before yesterday's purge/repair went wrong', not 'reconstruct the corpus from six months ago' - there is no six-months-ago yet. 14 days covers the realistic detection lag already seen on this project (BVL and etailment date issues surfaced days after collection, not same-day). Add keep_weekly/keep_monthly back once real weekly reports are going out and past-state reconstruction actually matters - it's a config change, not a code change. offbox_dir is a plain directory the OneDrive client already syncs - no rclone remote, no OAuth token. Set it to null to keep backups on this box only. warn_total_mb warns and never deletes: retention already bounds the normal case, so crossing it means an assumption broke.

monitoring._comment: Operational monitoring tables (src/monitoring.py, migration 007): pipeline_pass, discovery_source, fetch_event, body_attempt. Rows older than retention_days are pruned once a day when the daily pass is recorded - a rolling window for spotting problems early, not an archive. Runs, run_source and the corpus are never pruned by this.
